predecessors.note: The grant is the Peshwa's, so the land is also inside the maratha-empire shape until 1818. Other pages date it 1733 (Holkar, History of Indore) and give 1730 for Malhar Rao's appointment as chief of Malwa.

successors.note: Merged 16 June 1948 (Holkar page); Madhya Bharat created 28 May 1948. madhya-bharat needs a dossier (sa-06). The Indore State page gives accession 1 January 1948 (infobox) and 1 January 1950 (text).

capitals.name: Indore
capitals.note: The pargana headquarters had moved from Kampel to Indore by 1720 (Indore State page).

capitals.name: Maheshwar
capitals.note: Ahilyabai Holkar "moved the state's capital to Maheshwar in 1767".

capitals.name: Indore
capitals.note: "The capital was moved from Maheshwar to Indore on 3 November 1818."

rulers.name: Yashwant Rao Holkar I
rulers.note: His own page has him ruling and fighting the British from 1799; he died 28 October 1811.

rulers.name: Tukoji Rao Holkar III
rulers.note: Abdicated 1926 after being implicated in a murder case (Indore State page).

rulers.name: Yashwant Rao Holkar II
rulers.note: The Indore State page ends his reign on 15 August 1947; the Holkar page gives 1948.

The pages describe no extent between 1733 and 1818; the 1931 districts stand in for these years, so the shape is a floor, not the real Holkar dominion, which "lost much of their territory" in 1818 (Battle of Mahidpur page). Gap for a gap-filler: the Treaty of Mandsaur terms (the Treaty of Mandsaur and Treaty of Mandeswar pages would not load). Area about 23,500 km2 against 24,605 km2 (text) and 25,646 km2 (infobox) for 1931.

region.text: the 28 and a half parganas about Indore

ledger.note: 29 July 1732: the Peshwa grants Malhar Rao Holkar the Holkar state. "On 29 July 1732, Bajirao Peshwa-I granted Holkar State by granting 28 and a half parganas to Malhar Rao Holkar." Other pages say 1733 (Holkar: "granted 9 parganas in the vicinity of Indore"; History of Indore: 28 and one-half parganas in 1733) and 3 October 1730 for his appointment as chief of Malwa. The state is a member of the Maratha confederacy.
1767: Ahilyabai Holkar moves the capital from Indore to Maheshwar. "moved the state's capital to Maheshwar in 1767."

region.text: Delhi and the fort of Bharatpur, where the war with Lake was fought

ledger.note: 8 October 1804: Holkar marches on Delhi. "On 8 October 1804, to gain control over the emperor, Holkar marched towards Delhi"; the British "started hostilities against Yashwantrao Holkar on 6 April 1804" (Second Anglo-Maratha War page); "the failure of General Lake to conquer the fort of Bharatpur" is undated. The zone is my reading.

region.text: Delhi and the fort of Bharatpur

ledger.note: 24 December 1805: Holkar signs the Treaty of Rajghat. "signed a treaty with the British on 24 December 1805, at Rajghat"; "The British returned all his territory".

24 December 1805: Holkar gives up Tonk, Rampura and Bundi. "The Treaty of Rajghat, signed on 24 December 1805, forced Holkar to give up Tonk, Rampura, and Bundi to the British." The Yashwantrao Holkar page words it differently: the British "accepted his dominion over Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota, and Bundi" and he gave up "claims to Bundelkhand and territories to the north of Chambal river". These were outlying holdings or claims, not drawn in the keyframes; Rampura is ambiguous (Rampura-Bhanpura stays Holkar in 1931).
21 December 1817: the British beat Holkar at Mahidpur. "The battle of Mahidpur between Holkar and the British was fought on 21 December 1817."

6 January 1818: the Treaty of Mandeswar (Mandsaur) is signed; Holkar "accepted the British terms in totality" and the Holkar state became subsidiary to the British (Indore State page: British protectorate).

minus.text: the Holkar districts of the 1931 state: Indore, Maheshwar, Khargone and the Nimar side, Mehidpur, Rampura and Bhanpura (24,605 km2 on the page; scattered)

region.text: much of the Holkar territory: the pages name no region

ledger.note: 1818: the Holkars lose much of their territory. "The Holkars lost much of their territory to the British"; no opened page names the regions, so this event removes nothing from the drawn shape (the drawn shape is the post-1818 remnant).
3 November 1818: the capital returns from Maheshwar to Indore and the Indore Residency is established. "The capital was moved from Maheshwar to Indore on 3 November 1818."

region.text: the Holkar districts of the 1931 state: Indore, Maheshwar, Khargone and the Nimar side, Mehidpur, Rampura and Bhanpura (24,605 km2 on the page; scattered)

ledger.note: 16 June 1948: Indore merges into Madhya Bharat. "On 16 June 1948, the princely state of Indore, which the House of Holkar ruled, merged"; Madhya Bharat was created on 28 May 1948 after a covenant of 22 April 1948.

wars.name: Battle of Poona
wars.outcome: Holkar beats the combined armies of the Peshwa and Scindia on 25 October 1802 (Diwali); Baji Rao II flees to the British and signs the Treaty of Bassein in December.
wars.note: Second Anglo-Maratha War page: "In October 1802, the combined armies of Peshwa Baji Rao II and Scindia were defeated by Yashwantrao Holkar".

wars.name: Second Anglo-Maratha War (Holkar phase)
wars.outcome: British hostilities from 6 April 1804; Holkar fails at Delhi and Bharatpur; the Treaty of Rajghat of 24 December 1805 returns his territory and takes Tonk, Rampura and Bundi.

wars.name: Third Anglo-Maratha War (Holkar phase)
wars.outcome: British victory at Mahidpur on 21 December 1817; Treaty of Mandeswar of 6 January 1818 makes the Holkar state subsidiary.

certainty.note: The pages give parganas, towns and districts but no boundaries; the pre-1818 extent is not described at all.

A British subsidiary state with a recorded area (24,605 km2 in 1931) of scattered districts; the detached portions are drawn by circles around the district towns, so the edge is sharp in law but approximate in the drawing.

notes: Seven pages opened (Indore State, Holkar, Yashwantrao Holkar, Battle of Mahidpur, History of Indore, Second and Third Anglo-Maratha War). The pages do not describe the Holkar dominion before 1818 or the terms of the Treaty of Mandsaur (the pages Treaty of Mandsaur, Treaty of Mandeswar and Holkar dynasty returned url_not_found); the single post-1767 keyframe is the 1931 remnant used as a floor. A gap-filler should open the Mandsaur treaty terms and a page on Holkar Khandesh/Nimar holdings. Disagreements: founding year (29 July 1732 Indore State; 1733 Holkar, History of Indore; 1730/1731 other items), accession (1 January 1948 infobox, 1 January 1950 text, 1947 History of Indore, 16 June 1948 Holkar), Bundi at Rajghat (given up per Second Anglo-Maratha War; under his dominion per Yashwantrao Holkar). The state lies inside the maratha-empire Cliopatria shape until 1818. british-empire (sa-06) should record a vassal_start for indore-state at 6 January 1818 (to 1858), british-raj 1859-1947. Counterpart needing a dossier: madhya-bharat. Gazetteer lacks Khargone, Mehidpur, Rampura, Bhanpura, Bundi, Maheshwar as places; coordinates are used.
